entities.summary:
Stephan Bodecker was the 37th Bishop of Brandenburg and a Christian Hebraist, holding the position from 1432 to 1459. Born in Brandenburg, Prussia, he was a key figure in the development of the Brandenburgic Bible, a Latin translation of the Hebrew Bible commissioned by the Elector of Brandenburg. Bodecker's scholarly work spanned various fields, including biblical studies, theology, and language, and he was a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of 15th-century Brandenburg.

Bodecker's influence extended beyond his own region, as his translations and commentaries were widely disseminated throughout Europe. His most notable achievement, however, was his role in the creation of the Brandenburgic Bible, which helped to establish Brandenburg as a major center for biblical studies and Christian scholarship.

Stephan Bodecker's legacy can be seen in the continued importance of Brandenburg as a hub for biblical scholarship and Christian education. His contributions to the development of the Brandenburgic Bible have left a lasting impact on the field of biblical studies, and his work continues to be studied and appreciated by scholars today.

The Brandenburgic Bible, completed by Bodecker in 1459, contains a unique blend of scholarly insight and theological depth, making it a valuable resource for understanding the intellectual and cultural landscape of 15th-century Europe.
